Tags API

GET /workspaces/:id/tags lists a workspace's tags, each with how many things carry it, and GET /tags/:id lists everything carrying one tag, on every board. GET /boards/:id/tags shows the tags on one board, and POST /boards/:id/tags puts tags on its cards or takes them off, by name or by id, exactly as the Tag menu in the app does.

Updated October 25, 2026

A workspace's tags are read and applied here. Everything runs as you, so the API does with a tag exactly what the app does.

GET /workspaces/:id/tags

The workspace's tags, by name.

{
  "workspace_id": "5b2e…",
  "tags": [
    { "id": "0c9a…", "name": "Diner", "color": null, "entity_type": "setting",
      "description": null, "items": 14, "created_at": "2026-09-30T18:02:11Z" }
  ],
  "limit": 100, "offset": 0, "has_more": false
}

items is how many things carry the tag, the number the sidebar shows (null when it can't be counted just then). color is the one picked in the app, or null for the colour it gives the tag from its name. entity_type is one of character, setting, organization, concept (Topic, in the app) and thing, or null.

Parameter
nameJust the tag of that name, in any case
limitTags per page: 100 by default, at most 500
offsetWhere the page starts

GET /tags/:id

Everything carrying a tag, on every board in its workspace, the most recently tagged first: the tag's page, as data.

{
  "tag": { "id": "0c9a…", "name": "Diner", "workspace_id": "5b2e…", "…": "…" },
  "items": [
    { "kind": "card", "card_kind": "image", "board_id": "9f1c…", "board_name": "Locations",
      "card_id": "c-3", "title": "Booth, night", "excerpt": null,
      "auto": false, "tagged_at": "2026-10-20T09:14:02Z", "url": "https://…" },
    { "kind": "doc_page", "board_id": "9f1c…", "card_id": "d-4", "page_id": "p-2",
      "title": "Opening", "excerpt": "INT. DINER — NIGHT…", "auto": true, "…": "…" }
  ],
  "has_more": false
}

Each item's kind is card, group (with group_id and cards, how many cards it holds), board (a whole cluster), or doc_page (a page of a doc, with card_id and page_id). auto marks what was tagged automatically rather than by a person, and url opens it in the app. limit takes 100 by default, at most 500.

GET /boards/:id/tags

The tags on one board, and what carries each.

{
  "board_id": "9f1c…",
  "tags": [
    { "id": "0c9a…", "name": "Diner", "…": "…", "on_board": false,
      "cards": ["c-3", "c-7"], "groups": [], "pages": [{ "card_id": "d-4", "page_id": "p-2" }] }
  ],
  "url": "https://…"
}

on_board is true when the board itself carries the tag, and each list is in the order things were tagged. A card deleted from the board keeps its tags in case the delete is undone, and isn't listed; when the board can't be read just then, a note says deleted cards may be.

POST /boards/:id/tags

Puts tags on cards of this board and takes tags off them.

{ "card_ids": ["c-3", "c-7"], "add": ["Diner", "night exterior"], "remove": ["0c9a…"] }
Field
card_idsRequired. Up to 200 cards on this board
addTags to put on them, up to 10: names, or ids from the lists above
removeTags to take off them, up to 10, the same way

Send add, remove, or both. A name is matched in any case, and a leading # is ignored. Each works as the Tag… menu does:

  • A name the workspace has no tag for makes the tag, up to 80 characters. As a tag made in the app does, it then also goes on whatever else in the workspace says its name, marked auto.
  • A deleted tag's name brings that tag back with everything it was on, as recreating it in the app does.
  • Taking a tag off a card keeps it off that card for good: automatic tagging never puts it back there. Putting it on again yourself lifts that.
{
  "board_id": "9f1c…",
  "added": [
    { "id": "0c9a…", "name": "Diner", "…": "…", "created": false, "card_ids": ["c-7"] },
    { "id": "77d1…", "name": "night exterior", "…": "…", "created": true, "card_ids": ["c-3", "c-7"] }
  ],
  "removed": [{ "id": "3f2b…", "name": "Day", "…": "…", "card_ids": ["c-3"] }],
  "not_found": { "card_ids": [], "tags": [] },
  "url": "https://…"
}

Each tag's card_ids are the cards that changed: one that already had the tag, or never had the one taken off, isn't listed, so sending the same call twice changes nothing the second time. created marks a new tag and revived: true one brought back. An id that isn't a tag of this workspace, or a tag to take off that it doesn't have, is listed in not_found.tags, and a card that isn't on the board in not_found.card_ids.

Who can do what

Tags belong to a workspace. Its members read them; anyone who can edit the workspace tags things in it, and anyone else gets 403. Someone a board is shared with sees no tags. A board you can't open, or none of the cards on it, answers 404. Tagging reads the board to find its cards: when it can't be read just then, nothing is written and the answer is 503 room_unavailable, so try again.

Frequently asked questions

Does tagging a card by a new name make the tag?

Yes, as typing a new name into the app's Tag menu does. The new tag then also goes on whatever else in the workspace says its name, marked auto, as a tag made in the app does.

Will automatic tagging put back a tag I removed?

No. Taking a tag off a card over the API keeps it off that card for good, as removing it in the app does. Putting it back on yourself lifts that.

Who can tag things over the API?

Tags belong to a workspace. Its members can read them, and anyone who can edit the workspace can tag things in it, as in the app. Someone a board is shared with sees no tags.

Can an AI assistant tag cards?

Yes. The MCP server's list_tags and tag_cards tools are these endpoints, so an assistant can see how a workspace is tagged and tag the cards it is asked to.
